rows.evidence: Q1: Sections 2.2-2.4 - split-plot field experiment (2019-2020, Tongliao) comparing shallow-buried drip irrigation (SI) with under-mulch drip irrigation (MI) at three irrigation quotas, 18 plots, with 16S/ITS high-throughput sequencing of 0-20 and 20-40 cm soil. Q2: Section 3.1/Fig. 2 and Section 3.4/Figs. 5-6 and Discussion - bacterial OTU numbers in 0-20 cm were higher under SI than MI; LEfSe showed Holophagae, Thermoanaerobaculaceae, Microtrichales, Solirubrobacterales, Myxococcales etc. enriched in SI topsoil, which the authors describe as a relatively fertile habitat for beneficial microorganisms; Conclusion states SI enriched a rhizosphere-biased community important for nitrogen transformation.
rows.notes: The study supports the microbial-enrichment part of the claim with its own sequencing data. It does not measure plastic residue or economic/ecological benefits itself; those parts of the passage rest on cited literature in the Introduction/Discussion. Single method (amplicon sequencing; RDA with soil N is correlational, not an independent confirmation of enrichment). Mechanistic variables (soil moisture, temperature, film residue) are cited, not measured. One site, one soil, one crop, plot scale. No stated limitations; Table 4 gives means with letter groupings only, no dispersion measures. Differences by irrigation quota (significant at 50%) are reported as variation, not as a stated requirement.

notes: Full text appears complete. Table 1 labels appear scrambled (SI/MI rows do not match quota labels), but this does not affect ratings.
